title.narrative: Strengthening church advocacy to promote vaccination against COVID-19 in DRC

description.narrative: The Democratic Republic of Congo just like many other African country has been seriously hit by COVID 19. The 3rd wave has seriously swept the provinces of the eastern part of the country. Lately we have experienced some slight stability in the number of confirmed cases. However, “there is still this outstanding threat, and the risk is that if no measures are taken to strengthen protection measures, the next wave will even be more serious” as indicated by the Minister of Health Jean-Jacques Mbungani on October 21st 2021. The DRC launched a COVID-19 vaccination campaign on April 19, 2021 with the AstraZeneca vaccine. However, reception of this was very low from the community. Medical personnel have been among the most reluctant group of persons to get vaccinated even as they are at the front line. Generally speaking, the receptiveness of the vaccine in the DRC has remained low due to factors related to misinformation, cultural prejudices and plain lack of interest among the populace on the vaccine. Also, the DRC has been put on the list of countries that are at level 4 of COVID-19 and travellers from DRC are restricted to enter many EU and Asian countries. This means the situation is deteriorating drastically. The project will work with faith leaders to sensitise communities in Kinshasa, North Kivu (Goma), and South Kivu (Bukavu). This project will work with church structures and community radios to sensitize communities on COVID-19 prevention measures and support the Bishops in their efforts to pass the messages on the importance of taking vaccine. The vaccine messages will target those at risk, including elderly and those with pre-existing conditions. General sensitization will target youth as this will have ripple effects and be transmitted to the whole community. Building on the statement from the Bishops’ permanent committee, the project will work to amplify the voices of the bishops and influencers to model for the community and consequently encourage community to take vaccine.
